context:
Goal: the highest-grade PRs reach main first, in one wave, then the next grade when none is left.
Problem (rule): that idea needs a grade on each PR, and PRs carry none. Your pick that only lanes that are ready or one step from it bring main in already stands without a grade, so this question is only for the extra idea. It needs your word because it adds a new grade to every PR, or reuses one.
Based on (measured): triage read the roadmap record at 13:46 CST Nov 16: of 2,227 steps, 66 carry a `priority` field (now 32, next 28, later 1, low 5); every step has a `phase` and an `order`; 230 steps carry a `pr` field, so a PR reaches a grade only through its step. Most open PRs have no step (332 pulls with no step at the last recount).
Based on (read): the coordinator read no grade on any PR (relayed 13:46 CST).
Departs from: main — PRs have no grade and merge in the order they are ready; the options set a grade or leave it.
Meanwhile: lanes that are ready or near ready bring main in as you picked; nothing waits on this answer.

options.gain: No new field; every step already has a phase.
options.how: A PR's grade is the phase of the step that names it; a PR with no step is the lowest grade.
options.label: Use the step's phase (now, next, later) as the grade
options.lose: Most open PRs have no step, so most would be the lowest grade, and the grade says little.

options.gain: A grade you already set on purpose.
options.how: A PR's grade is its step's priority (now, next, later, low); everything else is ungraded and waits.
options.label: Use only the 66 steps that carry a priority field
options.lose: Only about 3 percent of steps are graded, so almost every PR is ungraded.

options.gain: No new field and no new work.
options.how: Nothing is built; lanes that are ready or near ready bring main in, as you picked.
options.label: No grade: the pick you already made is enough
options.lose: Higher-grade PRs get no extra push to main.

ref: your hedge on the main-in pick ("probably this and/or PRs of a certain priority grade are all brought to main at once ... if there's no high priority than all the medium priority ones"), relayed by the coordinator 13:46 CST Nov 16; ruling own-923-c-ready-lanes-bring-main-in

title: If PRs are brought to main together by priority grade, which grade should the system use?
why: Triage recommends c: your pick already keeps the ready queue clean; a grade would need a field on every PR and most PRs have no step. It is triage's recommendation, not owner-typed.
